answer: Require each identity to prove it sits at a distinct network location, checked by latency triangulation from several independent probes. A vine of identities sharing one server collapses to one location, because probes see the same round-trip times, while an island agent answers from its own corner of the map. A zephyr of keys spun up in one data centre cannot fake spread. An attacker chasing 1,000 fake agents must rent 1,000 nodes in distinct regions at about $10 a month each, roughly $10,000 a month, while one honest operator needs a single node.
